title: Husbands — Full-Film Source Audio Acoustic Reference
status: FULL_FILM_DERIVED_AUDIO_AND_CUE_DATA_PRESERVED — source WAV processed; 1,213 cue index, 1,213 cue acoustic screening records, 2,260-second dynamics timeline, and cast voice reference stored

source_audio.note: The original binary WAV is not stored in this JSON. The SHA-256 identifies the exact uploaded source. Derived full-cast aggregate profiles and compressed cue-level timing/voice features are stored in the two linked JSON references; these support future baseline and cue-window screening without re-uploading the WAV. Re-listening for nuanced emotion, breath, scene acting, or phoneme-level alignment would still require the audio itself.

source_alignment.alignment_note: Audio windows were aligned to the source subtitle cue timestamps and speaker_assignments.json. This is a first-pass alignment, not forced phoneme alignment.

analysis_method.vad: Dual-sensitivity WebRTC VAD: aggressiveness mode 2 (permissive) and mode 3 (conservative), 30 ms frames at 16 kHz
analysis_method.f0: Autocorrelation-based rough F0 estimate, 60–500 Hz search; profile summary excludes values outside 75–350 Hz to reduce octave and boundary errors
analysis_method.intensity: Frame RMS in dBFS over VAD-positive frames
analysis_method.spectral_brightness: Median spectral centroid over VAD-positive sampled frames
analysis_method.rate: English subtitle word count divided by total SRT subtitle-slot time. This is a subtitle-window density indicator, NOT true active-speech words per minute.
analysis_method.speaker_windows: Cue-level pass: each of the 1213 SRT cue windows was analyzed independently. Adjacent windows were not merged for this pass.
limits: Music, effects, reverberation, overlapping dialogue, and VAD false positives can influence acoustic measurements.
Merged same-speaker windows can include short inter-cue gaps and nearby speech; aggregate values are reference estimates, not clean isolated-stem measurements.
F0 estimates are approximate and can contain octave errors; low-sample characters must not be voice-matched from median F0 alone.
Acoustic features cannot reliably determine semantic emotion by themselves. Emotion labels must be confirmed against acting context and listening.
English word rate is not directly transferable to Mongolian dubbing; Mongolian syllable density, morphology, phrasing, and acting pauses must be considered independently.

Mode 2 and mode 3 produced materially different active-speech estimates, demonstrating that music/effects and low-energy speech make VAD duration uncertain. Do not use VAD duration as exact spoken duration or as a direct TTS speed target.

emotion_and_acting.rule: Do not infer an emotion label from pitch, loudness, or spectral brightness alone. Use audio plus scene context and dialogue semantics.
emotion_and_acting.vivienne_delivery_decisions: Use the existing user-confirmed emotion map. Narration defaults to natural, restrained delivery; D3 [angry] only for the user-approved genuinely angry cues, not for hurt, sarcasm, disgust, firmness, or sadness.
emotion_and_acting.other_characters: Emotion-by-cue annotation remains to be completed through scene-by-scene audition; current acoustic data provides a baseline for detecting changes in pitch, intensity, pace, and pauses.

dubbing_use.pace: Set cue-level rate and phrase timing from meaning and available dialogue window, not one constant speed. Preserve connected phrases across subtitle boundaries.
dubbing_use.timing: Use VAD-active speech estimates as initial timing references only. Final cue start/end and overlap decisions require listening against scene edits and neighboring speakers.
dubbing_use.voice_identity: Use the per-character median F0, IQR, RMS, and spectral centroid as rough reference ranges; prioritize human listening over numeric matching.
dubbing_use.emotion: Store emotion as a separate reviewed annotation with confidence and evidence. Keep source acoustic observations separate from interpretation.
dubbing_use.future_reuse: This JSON plus the English/Mongolian SRTs, speaker assignments, character registry, and emotion map is the reusable project reference. The WAV itself should not need to be re-uploaded for these baseline metrics.

next_required_passes: Human listening review of all high-priority timing and VAD-disagreement cues, using the original source dialogue and scene context.
Create a cue-level emotion and acting map for every speaking character: emotion, intensity, emphasis, breath, pause, vocal texture, phrase contour, and confidence/evidence.
Build clean non-overlapping reference excerpts for each character; small-sample characters require additional audition before voice casting.
Derive Mongolian dubbing pace targets per cue from the actual Mongolian syllable load, phrase meaning, source performance, and available dialogue window.
Review source subtitle overlaps and cue boundaries against the next speaker's actual onset; do not infer overrun solely from subtitle timestamps.

cue_level_screening.vad_mode2: permissive screening; likely includes some music/effects
cue_level_screening.vad_mode3: conservative screening; may miss low-energy or breathy speech
cue_level_screening.interpretation: Use mode 2/3 agreement as a confidence hint. Where the estimates differ substantially, require listening before deciding source onset, offset, pause, or speaking rate.
cue_level_screening.emotion_annotation: not automatically inferred; keep emotion review separate from acoustic measurements

cue_level_feature_file.description: Compressed per-cue source timing, conservative VAD active duration, rough F0 median, and RMS; join by cue order to the English/Mongolian SRT and speaker_assignments.json.

outputs.scope: All 1,213 cue windows; conservative VAD onset/end/active duration, rough median F0, median RMS; compressed binary records.
2,260 one-second windows across full 37:40.997 source; RMS, peak, zero-crossing rate and spectral centroid; includes whole-film signal summary.
All 1,213 cue IDs with start/end/duration, assigned speaker, English word count, inter-cue subtitle gap and display-WPM proxy; speaker aggregates.
Provisional all-character voice direction and existing aggregate acoustic profile notes.

limitations: Original WAV is intentionally not stored; its SHA-256 and technical metadata are retained.
One-second signal timeline is full mix and includes music/effects, not isolated character speech.
Cue VAD, F0 and RMS are screening estimates; not phoneme/word alignment or final TTS speed targets.
Cue display WPM and subtitle gaps are timing proxies, not verified spoken rate or true silence.
Emotion, breath, emphasis, phrase-level intonation and nuanced acting choices are not fully human-verified for every character/cue.
Word-level forced alignment and reliable phoneme durations have not been completed.
